title: Chapter 241: Who Is the Chairperson?
html:
The room fell utterly silent. Even the two most outspoken critics had nothing to say. A strange atmosphere settled over the dining table as the ten black-robed figures exchanged meaningful looks.

“If those aren’t enough, I have more.” Chen Ge was buying time for Zhang Ya. The other members did not interest him; his only objective that night was capturing Zhu Xiu.

“You still have other stories?”

The dining table fell silent again. The first man on the right scratched his head before turning to the fifth person on the left. “No. 5, are all his stories real?”

Everyone turned toward the enigmatic No. 5. The black robe shifted slightly, and an androgynous voice emerged from behind the mask. “I can detect no sign of deception in his words.”

Five true ghost stories... What kind of ‘remarkable’ life had he led?

“Looks like we have to redo the judging.” The man on the left moved his gaze to fall on the three other new members. “All of your stories are amazing, but we can only keep three new members.”

He placed his left hand on the table and extended one finger, beginning the second vote. The others decided just as quickly. Six fingers pointed toward No. 1.

“You got more than half of the votes.” The man on the left turned to No. 1. “I’m sorry, No. 1, but you can leave now.”

“Leave?” No. 1 panicked and tried to object, but the man on the left cut him off.

“You can come back next Wednesday.”

A visibly anxious No. 1 was ushered from the room. The bird-masked man was waiting outside and appeared surprised that Chen Ge had not been selected.

“Follow me.” The birdman led No. 1 away and closed the door.

Once the door closed, the first man on the left finished his thought. “Provided you survive until next Wednesday.”

A scream immediately erupted in the corridor, followed by the thud of something heavy striking the floor. No. 2’s legs trembled. Four people had voted against him; two more, and he would have been outside instead.

“Don’t worry. The rejected newcomer will live on in another form.” The first man on the left softened his voice. “Welcome to the Ghost Stories Society. You will be Nos. 11, 12, and 13, respectively.”

Because Chen Ge had arrived last, he became No. 13. The blood within his shadow grew more distinct. Having survived the first wave of danger, he relaxed slightly. The Ghost Stories Society was the Third Sick Hall’s hidden mission and connected to the world behind the door. Its reward was likely Men Nan’s primary personality, a Red Specter capable of controlling that ‘door.’

“I have a question,” said the woman now designated No. 12, her voice as emotionally restrained as before. “The flyer claims I can find relief from my pain. How?”

“Don’t worry. Everyone here has known profound suffering. We are all patients, and this society exists to help its members seek salvation.” The man on the right studied her. “Once you tell three true ghost stories, we will devise a solution tailored to your condition.”

Chen Ge listened in silence. He had initially dismissed the society as a circle of lunatics indulging one another and had not expected it to possess an underlying purpose.

“How do you expect real ghost stories to happen so often?” As she spoke, the woman glanced warily at Chen Ge.

“Ghost stories surround us; you simply haven’t paid attention. Everything written on the flyer is true, and many members have found salvation here. One woman had been abused by her stepfather since childhood. He whipped her and held her underwater until she developed a profound fear of water. After coming to us, she was cured.”

“How did you cure her?”

“Very simply. We forced her stepfather underwater and let her destroy the source of her fear with her own hands.”

“That’s it?”

“Yes, that simple. Every one of us is ill, though our conditions and their causes differ. Don’t worry. When your turn comes, we will design a treatment especially for you.” The man on the right spoke with calm confidence, and Chen Ge imagined a reassuring face beneath the mask.

“You already know the condition. Once you can tell three real ghost stories, you can demand something from us, or you can choose to leave.” The man laughed and added with humor, “And it’ll be real that time.”

“Three ghost stories?” The woman lowered her head to think.

Their conversation shocked Chen Ge. That isn’t therapy—it’s murder. Then again, only madmen could devise treatment like this.

Chen Ge’s gaze swept over everyone at the table. The patients from the Third Sick Hall were probably among them!

The devil from Room 10 and Wu Fei from Room 9 were probably the Ghost Stories Society’s founders. Both were patients themselves, and Room 10 contained a record of the devil’s suffering. In a sense, no one could empathize with these disturbed people more deeply.

When medicine failed to relieve their pain, they had begun treating themselves—using madness to offer salvation to the mad.

“Every newcomer may ask one question.” The man looked at No. 2 and Chen Ge. “Which of you would like to go first?”

“I’ve run into some trouble recently. The police are watching me.” No. 2 raised his head and surveyed the room. No one reacted; such trouble appeared commonplace here.

“I can probably guess your problem—another desperate man backed against a wall.” The man on the left reclined in his chair. “We cannot make that problem disappear, but the society can give you somewhere to hide. You may even remain here forever.”

No. 2 nodded, slightly disappointed.

The room turned back to Chen Ge. “What is your question?”

“My question is simpler.” A chill ran down Chen Ge’s spine. He had never imagined that monsters from behind the door and patients from the Third Sick Hall would cooperate to create something like this. After a long pause, he asked directly, “Who is the society’s chairperson?”

“The chairperson?”

The black robes went silent once more. They looked at one another, and in the end, it was the first man on the left who spoke. “Change your question.”

“You cannot tell me?” The more they wanted to hide it, the more interested Chen Ge was.

“It’s not that,” the man on the right said. “We know the chairperson is among the ten of us, but which of us it is, we ourselves do not know.”
